sections.contenu_markdown: A quick test distinguishes possessive pronouns from possessive adjectives: does a noun follow? If not, use the pronoun form (yours, not your).

A possessive pronoun (mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs) stands alone, replacing a noun already mentioned, and is never followed by another noun; a possessive adjective (my, your, his, her, our, their) must always be followed by a noun.

etapes.action: Check if a noun follows the blank
etapes.justification: The sentence ends right after the blank, no noun follows.
Standing alone requires a possessive pronoun, not an adjective.

items.erreur_markdown: Using 'your' alone without a following noun.
items.pourquoi_faux: 'Your' is a possessive adjective that must always be followed by a noun (e.g. 'your books'); used alone, it is grammatically incomplete.
items.correction_markdown: Check systematically: if no noun follows, use the possessive pronoun (mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs).

items.solution_markdown: mine (no noun follows, so the pronoun form is required).

items_markdown: Possessive pronoun (yours, mine...) stands alone, no noun follows
Possessive adjective (your, my...) always followed by a noun
